name: digestif-relay
description: The Digestif relay: a mailbox that mirrors one circle. It accepts signed envelopes from admitted keys and serves them by cursor. It checks envelopes and need not read a body. Every request is signed by a device key and carries the Digestif-Key, Digestif-Timestamp, Digestif-Nonce and Digestif-Signature headers (on the bootstrap read, GET /v0/invites/:invite_key, Digestif-Key is the invite key); see docs/protocol.md for canonical encoding, hashing, request signing and the admission fold.

kind.description: Circle-state kinds go to every admitted reader; content kinds go to readers whose join epoch is at or before the envelope's epoch. A node ignores kinds it does not know.

values.name: dinner
values.description: Circle state. A host names guests and their invite keys. The founding dinner is the circle root.

values.name: join
values.description: Circle state. A guest's identity key, signed by their invite key, and first device key, signed by the identity key.

values.name: device
values.description: Circle state. A device key (laptop, mail key, later a phone), signed by the identity key.

values.name: revoke
values.description: Circle state. Revokes a device key (signed by the identity key) or an identity key (signed by itself or the host who admitted it).

values.name: card
values.description: Circle state. The member's name, their agent's name and their encryption public key.

values.name: relay
values.description: Circle state. Announces a relay: its URL and, for a mailing relay, its encryption key.

values.name: summary
values.description: Content. The nightly note.

values.name: question
values.description: Content. Directed to one member, sealed to their encryption key.

values.name: answer
values.description: Content. Directed, sealed.

values.name: proposal
values.description: Content. Directed, sealed.

values.name: digest
values.description: Content. Sealed to the member's own key and the mailing relay's key.

values.name: retract
values.description: Content. Hides a target the same author wrote; relays drop the target's body and keep its envelope as a tombstone.

values.name: identity
values.description: Derived from the recovery phrase, never stored. Signs only device and revoke messages.

values.name: device
values.description: A machine's key. Signs everything else.

values.name: mail
values.description: A chainless device key whose pre-signed answers ride in the digest. Any unseen sequence number is accepted; the fork rule does not apply.

values.name: duplicate
values.description: The relay already holds an envelope with this hash. Appends are idempotent.

values.name: malformed
values.description: The envelope or body does not parse, or kind and body disagree.

values.name: bad_signature
values.description: The envelope, the request or a signature inside a circle-state body does not verify.

values.name: not_admitted
values.description: The signing key is not in the admitted set, or was revoked.

values.name: stale_request
values.description: The timestamp is outside the skew window.

values.name: sequence_regression
values.description: The sequence number is not greater than the last this relay holds for a chained key.

values.name: fork
values.description: A different envelope with the same author and sequence number is already held. The relay keeps the first and the node surfaces the fault.

values.name: too_large
values.description: The envelope with its body exceeds the size cap.

values.name: rate_limited
values.description: The device has reached its daily append cap.

values.name: wrong_circle
values.description: The envelope does not fold from this relay's circle root.

values.name: retract_not_author
values.description: A retract names a target written by a different identity.

envelope.description: One signed, immutable message. The signature covers the canonical encoding of every field but signature itself, and body_hash binds the body, so a relay can drop a retracted body and the envelope still verifies.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Envelope version. 0 for v0. Bumped by protocol changes.

fields.name: author
fields.description: The signing key, ed25519:<base64url>. A device or mail key; an invite key on a join's outer envelope; the host's device key on a dinner.

fields.name: seq
fields.description: Strictly increasing per chained author. Gaps are expected only for mail keys.

fields.name: prev
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the author's previous envelope. Absent on an author's first envelope. For a mail key, the hash of the ask being answered.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: The author's clock. Informational; ordering comes from seq per author and relay_id per relay.

fields.name: epoch
fields.description: Increments on every join. A newcomer reads content from their join epoch forward.

fields.name: body_hash
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the canonical encoding of the body.

fields.name: signature
fields.description: ed25519 signature by author, base64url.

signed_envelope.description: What a node appends and a relay stores: the envelope and the body beside it.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body, whose shape is fixed by kind (docs/protocol.md). Absent when a retract dropped it or the reader may not see it.

fields.name: relay_id
fields.description: Assigned by this relay, only ever increasing. Cursors are per relay; nodes dedupe by envelope hash across relays.

fields.name: hash
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the canonical envelope including its signature.

fields.name: next
fields.description: Pass as after to fetch the next page. Absent when the reader is caught up.

admitted_key.description: One key in this relay's admitted set, the result of folding dinner, join, device and revoke from the circle root.

fields.name: identity
fields.description: The identity key this key belongs to (itself, for an identity key).

fields.name: admitted_at
fields.description: relay_id of the message that admitted it.

fields.name: join_epoch
fields.description: The member's join epoch, the floor for the content they may fetch.

fields.name: revoked_at
fields.description: relay_id of the revoke, when revoked.

fields.name: root
fields.description: sha256:<hex> of the founding dinner envelope this relay is configured with.

fields.name: epoch
fields.description: The current epoch by this relay's fold.

fields.name: max_envelope_bytes
fields.description: Envelope plus body. Default 65536.

fields.name: max_appends_per_device_per_day
fields.description: Default 500, UTC day.

fields.name: max_page_size
fields.description: Default 500.

fields.name: skew_seconds
fields.description: Default 3600.

operations.description: Append one envelope. A dinner or join is accepted when the signatures inside it verify against the fold so far (the bootstrap rule); every other append requires an admitted, unrevoked device or mail key as both request signer and envelope author. Idempotent by envelope hash.

401.description: The request signature, timestamp, nonce or signer failed: bad_signature, stale_request, replayed_nonce, not_admitted.

422.description: The envelope was refused: malformed, bad_signature, not_admitted, sequence_regression, fork, too_large, wrong_circle, retract_not_author.

operations.description: Everything after a cursor, in relay_id order. Circle-state kinds in full; content kinds whose epoch is at or after the reader's join epoch, without bodies the reader may not see. Requires an admitted device key.

The bootstrap read: the dinner envelope, with its body, that names this invite key. Signed by the invite key itself as Digestif-Key, so only whoever holds the invite code can read it, and answered only while the invite is unspent and unexpired. The guest's app reads it before it is admitted, to learn the dinner hash its join names and every relay to append the join to.

parameters.name: invite_key
parameters.description: The invite key, ed25519:<base64url>, as the dinner lists it.

401.description: bad_signature, stale_request or replayed_nonce, or a Digestif-Key other than the invite key in the path.

404.description: No dinner in this relay's fold names the invite key, or the invite was spent or has expired. One answer for all three, so the read says nothing about invites its caller does not hold.

operations.description: The circle root, current epoch, admitted keys and limits. Requires an admitted device key, so a relay's contents are readable by members and nobody else.
